newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court leaves to states internal tax and trade regulations.
newsitem.headline: Court leaves to states internal tax and trade regulations.

text.p: The European Court of Justice decided on Thursday member states may require the presentation of documents for goods transported within national borders.

Community tax rules abolishing fiscal frontiers between European Union members do not prevent national rules which require goods, travelling within the confines of that state, to be documented for tax purposes.

A 1978 Italian law requires goods in transport within Italy to be accompanied by fiscal documents. After Community rules enacted in 1993 abolished fiscal control between member states, Italy stated its intention to maintain its rule for domestic transport, and for goods from non-EU countries.

This issue arose in the context of a dispute between Italian tax authorities, and a door-to-door produce salesman. The salesman was fined for failing to draw up, or drawing up incorrectly, documents in respect of goods transported within Italy.
The court considered the intent of relevant provisions of the Sixth VAT directive in the context of the aims pursued by the legislation.

"The directive's main purpose is to complete the internal market, to eliminate fiscal frontiers ... and to abolish fiscal controls ... between member states. The purpose of the directive is not, however, to harmonize or to simplify formalities relating to purely internal transactions," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)

"Value added tax - Interpretation of article 22(8) of the Sixth directive (77/388/EEC) as amended by directive 91/680/EEC - Equal treatment of domestic transactions and transactions carried out between member states by taxable persons"
Reference from the Commissione Tributaria di Primo Grado di Bolzano (Italy) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of article 22(8) the Sixth directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1), as amended by article 28h inserted by Council directive 91/680/EEC of 16 December 1991 supplementing the common system of value added tax and amending directive 77/388/EEC with a view to the abolition of fiscal frontiers (OJ 1991 L 376, p. 1)

Article 22(8) the Sixth directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment, as amended by article 28h inserted by Council directive 91/680/EEC of 16 December 1991 supplementing the common system of value added tax and amending directive 77/388/EEC with a view to the abolition of fiscal frontiers, is to be interpreted as not precluding a national rule requiring accompanying documents to be drawn up in respect of goods transported within the confines of the member state concerned.
